subject: Telemetry deep-dive & next tests after demo
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gonzalez <alice@dataware.io>, ops-team@dataware.io
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T15:02:00Z
Subject: Telemetry deep-dive & next tests after demo

Hi Alice / Dataware ops team,

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to see your production profile and the two demo flows. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the concrete telemetry/observability asks so we can scope the competitive tests (Redwood vs hyperscaler endpoints) and the operational checks the engineering team wants to validate.

Quick recap of what you asked for during the call:
- Token-level cost/usage exports (daily + per-request)
- Traces that correlate request ID -> model invocation spans (OpenTelemetry preferred)
- Prometheus metrics for model instance-level latency and queue depth
- Support for prefix/KV cache effectiveness metrics (cache hits/misses)

Proposed next tests (we can iterate):
1) Baseline throughput/latency: run your 90/10 read/write mix against Redwood-hosted endpoint and one hyperscaler-managed endpoint (you mentioned your Vertex proof-of-concept). Measure p50/p95/p99 for 1k, 5k, and 20k concurrent short requests.
2) Cache measurement: replay a representative prefix-heavy workload (we'll accept a 10k request sample) to measure effective token savings and token-cost delta with and without prefix caching.
3) Tracing fidelity: validate OpenTelemetry trace propagation across request -> model -> backend, with sampling at 100% for the test window so you can see full span hierarchy.
4) Failure/retry behavior: induce transient GPU warm-start and network hiccups to compare graceful degradation and fallback routing.

What we need from you to move forward:
- Representative request trace sample (10k lines or a 48-hour sample) — safe to obfuscate PII.
- Temporary test service account or short-lived API key for a dedicated test project.
- Confirmation of the hyperscaler endpoints you want included.

I've attached a short checklist and the telemetry fields we recommend (redwood_telemetry-ask.pdf). If this looks good, I propose we schedule a 90-minute ops deep-dive next week (engineering + SRE). Sergio and Marissa will run the instrumentation and coordinate test windows.

Next steps:
- Alice: share sample traces and preferred test dates
- Dataware ops: grant temporary test creds or confirm manual run approach
- Redwood: send detailed test plan and timeslots

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192

[Attachment: redwood_telemetry-ask.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Alice Gonzalez <alice@dataware.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-team@dataware.io, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T17:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Telemetry deep-dive & next tests after demo

Ben — thanks for the clear summary. This matches our expectations. I've uploaded a token-sampled trace bundle and a short CSV of representative requests. The team scrubbed sensitive content.

Attached: dataware_sample_traces.zip (contains sample_traces.json, request_samples.csv)

We're comfortable with Redwood running the tests against a staging copy of our traffic (same request shapes, redacted). We can also run an identical workload against the hyperscaler endpoint if you provide the test harness.

Availability: Jul 27–29 (US PDT) for a 90-min window — please confirm.

Also: we need clarity on how Redwood will surface token-level chargebacks in the telemetry — daily exports or per-request? For procurement we'll need a template export to ingest into our billing reconciliation.

— Alice
VP, Infrastructure 
Dataware Analytics
alice@dataware.io

[Attachment: dataware_sample_traces.zip (application/zip)]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alice Gonzalez <alice@dataware.io>, ops-team@dataware.io
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-23T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Telemetry deep-dive & next tests after demo

Perfect — thanks for sending the sample traces, Alice. We reviewed the bundle and it looks usable. A few clarifications and a narrower test matrix so engineering can scope resource needs: 

Test matrix (short):
- Throughput buckets: 1k, 5k, 20k concurrent short requests
- Payload types: short prompt (avg 120 tokens), long prompt (avg 1,200 tokens)
- Endpoints: Redwood-hosted (r-inference-std), Hyperscaler A (vertex-stub), Hyperscaler B (hypothetical bedrock-stub) — we won't need live commercial accounts for hyperscalers if you run parallel harnesses and share results; better if you give us a test endpoint.
- Metrics collected: p50/p95/p99 latencies, per-request token counts, total token spend estimate, cache hit ratio, traces (OTel), and Prometheus scrape for instance metrics every 10s.

On token-level exports: Redwood can provide both a per-request CSV export (request_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, model, cost_estimate) and a daily summary. For the test, we will enable the per-request export and produce a sample ingestion script compatible with your billing team.

Security: for the staging run we prefer a short-lived test key. If you prefer to run the hyperscaler comparison from your side and share the raw CSVs, that's fine — we just need consistent request IDs to correlate traces.

Proposed schedule: Jul 28 at 09:00 PDT for the joint run (90 minutes). Please confirm by end of day Jul 24.

I'll drop the initial test plan CSV to the drive link and attach a minimal ops checklist. Sergio — can you own the instrumentation and run orchestration? Karthik — please review the failure/retry scenarios and confirm required infra.

Ben

[Attachment: redwood-testplan-ops.csv (text/csv)]

- Create a runbook for the Jul 28 window and post to the drive (will include rollback and failure cutover steps).
- Sergio: please prepare OTEL collector config and ensure 100% sampling for spans during the test window.
- Karthik: prepare the failure injection script (network delay / GPU cold-start) and confirm the infra controls.

I'll loop in Eng SRE slack channel and post a short checklist. Ben / Alice: I expect we'll be able to produce the per-request CSV export and example ingestion script by EOD Jul 27.

Marissa Cole
Product Ops
marissa@redwood.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-07-25T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Telemetry deep-dive & next tests after demo

Thanks team — confirmed for Jul 28 09:00 PDT. I've created the initial test plan and uploaded to the drive (link in related_links). Highlights:
- We'll run three iterations per throughput bucket, capture OTEL spans, and produced consolidated CSVs.
- Expect per-request CSV to include: request_id, start_ts, end_ts, model_name, tokens_in, tokens_out, estimated_cost_usd, cache_hit
- We'll also include a trace sample and a Prometheus dump for the test window.

Alice: when you share the test key / endpoint please also add a small sample of the authentication headers so we can match the traces. If you'd rather we run from your harness, share the harness script and we'll adapt.

Looking forward — Sergio
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
